title: Matrix Chain Multiplication
statement:
# Matrix Chain Multiplication

**Difficulty:** Hard

**Patterns:** Dynamic Programming → DP on Intervals

**Source:** Classic interview problem (not on LeetCode) — statement authored for this dataset.

**Reference:** https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/matrix-chain-multiplication-dp-8/

---

## Problem Statement

Given an array `dims` of length `n + 1` describing `n` matrices, where matrix
`i` has dimensions `dims[i-1] x dims[i]`, return the **minimum number of scalar
multiplications** needed to compute the product of the whole chain.

Multiplying a `p x q` matrix by a `q x r` matrix costs `p * q * r`.

This is the archetypal interval DP: `dp[i][j]` is the best cost for the chain
`i..j`, minimised over every position of the final split.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: dims = [40,20,30,10,30]
Output: 26000
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: dims = [10,20,30]
Output: 6000
```

**Constraints:**

- `2 <= dims.length <= 100`
- `1 <= dims[i] <= 500`
approach: dp[i][j] is the cheapest way to multiply matrices i..j; the last multiplication happens at some k, costing dims[i-1] * dims[k] * dims[j].
